newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Bunds lively as technicals sour futures.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Bunds lively as technicals sour futures.

text.p: Trade in Bund options on LIFFE quickened on Tuesday and volatility scuttled higher as the underlying futures fell below their recent trading range, brokers said.
Impending U.S. wage data added a nervous tone to the negative technical picture, they added.
"We've come out of the trading range we were holding onto and people have been getting a little more active," said at a broker at a London brokerage.
March Bund futures were quoted at 100.79 at 1212 GMT, down 36 basis points from Monday's settlement and well below the 101.05 low that has been in place since January 15.
March T-bond futures were quoted at 109-29, up 4/32 from their close in Chicago on Monday, when they dipped to 109-19, their lowest level since October 25.
The broker quoted implied volatility of March Bund options at 6.2/6.5 percent, compared with official LIFFE data of 5.7 percent at the close on Monday.
There was little activity in April or May options but June volatility was quoted at 6.1/6.2 percent versus 5.7 percent at Monday's close according to LIFFE.
Among trades, a U.S. bank sold 2,000 lots of March 98.50 strike calls and bought 1,000 lots of March par puts, adding to the 3,000 par puts they bought on Monday, the broker said.
A British investment house was busy in June, selling 800 lots of 97.00 puts at the same time as selling the 99.50 future.
"They were selling the puts and selling the futures as a hedge against it, into the vol, which was 6.74 percent, a bit higher up the skew," he said.
Mourad Amellel, options trader at Transoptions Finance in London, said investors were active in puts ahead of the U.S. fourth quarter employment cost index (ECI) due at 1330 GMT.
"A lot of people have been buying puts," he said. "They are scared about this figure. Either the bonds will rise two points or lose two points."
Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the ECI to have risen 0.9 percent in the fourth quarter after a 0.6 percent rise in the third quarter.
